draft:
We are writing to inform you of a new investment in Casa Verde Group, a Milan-headquartered premium European homeware and kitchenware specialist. The transaction values Casa Verde at an enterprise value of EUR 1.85 billion, representing 12.4x trailing twelve months EBITDA of EUR 149 million. We will invest EUR 720 million of equity for an 84 percent stake.

Casa Verde was founded in 1973 by Giovanni Esposito as a single shop in Milan. The Company today operates 184 retail stores across Italy, France, Spain, and Germany, alongside an e-commerce platform that contributes 31 percent of group revenue and a wholesale business serving design-led independent retailers across Europe. Revenue in 2025 was EUR 612 million with EBITDA margins of 24.3 percent.

The investment thesis rests on five pillars. First, Casa Verde is a category leader in the EUR 38 billion European premium homeware market — a structurally attractive category growing at 4 to 5 percent annually. Second, store unit economics are exceptional, with average four-wall EBITDA margins of 22 percent and 2.4-year payback on new openings. Third, there is a well-defined international expansion runway: the Company has executed successful launches in France, Spain, and Germany, and we plan to enter the UK, Netherlands, and Nordics. Fourth, own-brand product penetration has grown from 38 percent in 2020 to 54 percent in 2025, with continued runway to 70 percent contributing material gross margin expansion. Fifth, the Atelier 73 concept — currently 18 stores — has the potential to become a meaningful third growth pillar.

Our value creation plan envisages revenue growth from EUR 612 million to approximately EUR 1.04 billion by 2031, a 9.2 percent CAGR. EBITDA is expected to grow from EUR 149 million to approximately EUR 295 million with margins expanding to 28.4 percent. The base case generates 2.7x MOIC and 22 percent gross IRR.

The principal risks are international expansion execution (the UK and Nordic launches contribute the largest single bucket of growth), consumer discretionary exposure (Germany has been notably weak), family transition (Marco Esposito will step back, with Elena Conti taking over as CEO), real estate exposure on 167 of the 184 stores, and wholesale channel concentration. Each is well-understood and reflected in our planning.

This transaction has been negotiated bilaterally over an 18-month period with the Esposito family. The agreed enterprise value reflects a discount of approximately 10 to 15 percent to fair competitive value, in line with the family's stated preference for a partner over the highest price. We have completed comprehensive diligence (Bain on commercial, Deloitte on financial, Latham on legal, ERM on ESG) and the conclusions are circulated separately.
